Lumen & Silt

Thesis Focus
Post-extractive geography, mineral memory, and computational ecology in deep coastal strata.
01 / 08
Curatorial Thesis · Core Argument

Industrial runoff and undersea fiber optic cables form a single contemporary geology. Artworks in this biennale operate as calibrated sensors, registering post-extractive transformation rather than mourning it.

01. Subterranean Archives

Drilling cores, deep sediment extraction, and heavy metal deposits decoded through sculptural and sonic physical archives.

02. Hydrological Signals

Tidal telemetry, underwater acoustic transducers, and water-table simulation modeling living infrastructure networks.

03. Post-Carbon Poetics

Ecological remediation, living algae bioreactors, and indigenous restorative practices challenging extractive capitalism.

02 / 08
Spatial Architecture · 4 Pavilions
Four
Thresholds
A locked 75-minute physical progression through Arsenale’s historic naval cordage. Each pavilion isolates acoustic bleed while transitioning from blinding daylight to absolute darkness.
I

Atrium: Suspension

Monumental saline textile architecture suspended from 14m steel trusses. Ambient tidal acoustic field greeting visitors immediately past ticketing.

II

North Gallery: The Core Sample

Heavy industrial vitrines housing deep-sea drilling cores, radioactive glaze ceramics, and rare-earth material extraction documentation.

III

South Hall: Hydrological Drift

16-channel spatialized video and sub-bass hydrophone array. Visitors navigate elevated timber walkways over reflective brackish water basins.

IV

Vaults: Terminal Bloom

Subterranean brick vaults hosting living bioluminescent algae bioreactors, anaerobic fermentation sculptures, and mycorrhizal computational sound.

Publishing & Civic Discourse
Public
Life

The exhibition extends beyond physical gallery walls via international publishing partnerships, symposia, and permanent educational endowments for the region.

Exhibition Monograph

Hardcover Catalog (Hatje Cantz)

320-page trilingual volume featuring scholarly contributions by Donna Haraway, Keller Easterling, and Édouard Glissant archive curators.

Vernissage Summit

Symposium: "Extraction & Frequency"

3-day interdisciplinary conference convening artists, marine geologists, and computational theorists at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale.

Civic Engagement

Free Tuesdays & School Transit Bursary

$180,000 allocated to subsidize regional transit and free museum admission for over 14,000 public high school students.
